messages:
maya: noticing ~3x error rate from gateway -> model routing since 18:00 UTC, latency spike on the low-cost route. Can we flip the panic button route pin to route-all:high-priority for affected customer segments?

maya: current pattern looks like header mismatch + transient model OOMs, not upstream capacity. want a quick containment rather than full rollback.

devin: oncall here. agree containment first. which route matcher do you want to pin? the header-based fast-path or the fallback by route-id?

maya: pin the header fast-path off. run fallback route-id=high-priority using the emergency routing toggle. This should preserve SLA for paying customers.

maya: example toggle command (console + api):
```http
POST /api/v1/feature-flags/routing/toggle
Authorization: Bearer xxxxx
Content-Type: application/json
{ "toggle": "panic_route_pin", "value": "route-id:high-priority", "scope": "global", "reason": "prod spike 18:00 UTC" }
```

devin: running toggle now. tagging @oncall-bot to record action.

oncall-bot: action_recorded: user=devin toggle=panic_route_pin value=route-id:high-priority ts=1845012412

devin: toggled. response: 200 OK, new active routes: [high-priority, legacy-fallback]. rolling traffic shift started.

alex: heads-up — this will increase tokens on dedicated capacity by ~12% for the next 10m per telemetry forecast. quotas in console might spike. Should we pre-approve burst?

maya: yes approve burst for 20m for affected customers. devops, please monitor quota burn.

sam: updating runbook note under "route panic" with exact commands and fallback steps. also adding who to ping for a rollback.

jun: checking dashboards — run these queries for quick health checks: 
`sum(increase(requests_total[5m])) by (route)`
`rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{quantile="0.99"}[2m])`
`sum(rate(errors_total[1m])) by (route)`

jun: setting a short-lived alert on p99 > 450ms OR error_rate > 2% for the high-priority route.

devin: telemetry shows p50 stable, p99 lower after flip, error-rate dropping from 3.1% -> 0.8% over 90s. so far so good.

alex: console quota shows burst used ~9% of dedicated pool. fine for now but keep an eye.

maya: ok when do we plan to unpin? policy: keep pinned until 30m stable or until SRE says safe. propose 30m check-in.

devin: noted. I'll annotate incident timeline and leave toggle active. rollback procedure if errors spike: run `POST /api/v1/feature-flags/routing/toggle {value: "auto"}` then run `kubectl rollout restart gateway --namespace=prod` if routes don't reconcile within 60s.

sam: added rollback steps + exact `kubectl` commands in runbook. also added step to update customer-facing status if we need a longer mitigation.

jun: dashboard panels updated and alert muted for non-prod noise. created a temporary graph showing route-weight distribution.

oncall-bot: incident_log: incident=route_spike_1845012345 status=mitigation_in_progress assignee=devin ts=1845012583

maya: thanks team. keeping this thread as canonical for the action. will post final status at 18:40 UTC (30m).

devin: will follow-up at 18:40 UTC with metrics snapshot and decision.

maya: 18:40 update — metrics stable, p99 < 420ms, error-rate < 1%. unpin window scheduled at 18:55 UTC with a staged rollback if problems recur.

devin: unpin scheduled. leaving toggle active until handover in case traffic oscillates.

sam: runbook entry link: https://internal/doc/runbooks/route-panic (added).

maya: closing thread after handover. thanks all :thumbsup:
